task: Quantitative model of the deglutition (swallowing) motor sequence: (1) the pharyngeal-phase airway-protection TIMING window reduced to an interval-containment margin (deglutitive apnea duration minus UES-relaxation/bolus-dwell duration), forced against a no-sequenced-CPG adversary (simultaneous onset -- deterministic fail for any positive closure latency; randomized onset -- Monte Carlo + closed-form analytic cross-check, 79.6-96.6% failure across a 5-point window sweep); (2) esophageal peristaltic velocity + striated/smooth transition-zone geometry, cross-checked for whole-esophagus transit-time consistency against the real ~8-10s anchor (3 decorrelated corroborations) after a self-caught domain-mismatched naive model overshot by 67-109%; (3) an achalasia adversary reproducing the real Chicago-Classification IRP>15mmHg criterion (Ghosh et al. 2007, corroborated by a 2nd independent cohort) plus a divergent (mathematically inf) transit time under aperistalsis; (4) the real, decorrelated Martino et al. 2005 population dysphagia/aspiration/pneumonia-risk anchor, cross-checked against 2 real videofluoroscopy cohorts with a disclosed, UNRESOLVED cross-study tension on which specific timing parameter predicts aspiration.
confidence_tier: mechanism-plausibility, geometrically-forced, with multiple directly-measured, cross-corroborated calibration anchors. The core F1 margin mechanism (apnea duration minus UES-relaxation duration) is built from 2 fully independent primary measurements (Martin et al. 1994; Kahrilas et al. 1988 -- different labs/methods/cohorts) and its adversary consequences are forced, not asserted: simultaneous onset fails deterministically for any positive closure latency; randomized onset fails at empirical rates matching a closed-form analytic geometric-overlap prediction to within 0.4 percentage points across a 5-point window sweep. The esophageal transit-time claim (8.00s) is corroborated by 3 decorrelated sources (the task's own 8-10s anchor; Pouderoux et al. 1997's independently-measured velocity times a textbook length; Silva et al. 2018's independent HRM distal-latency percentile, n=32). The achalasia IRP threshold (15mmHg, Ghosh et al. 2007, n=473) is corroborated by a 2nd fully independent cohort (Silva et al. 2018, n=32, different country/instrument) whose own healthy-population IRP 95th percentile (15.45mmHg) lands almost exactly at the same cutoff. The weakest-anchored piece is Part D's lesion-severity margin sweep, explicitly disclosed as an illustrative (not independently fit) qualitative bridge to the real Martino et al. 2005 population numbers. One tier below a subject-specific in-vivo measurement (no swallowing/manometry study exists for subject2 in this repo) -- comparable to this repo's own MECHANISM_PULMONARY_SURFACTANT.md and MECHANISM_THYROID_AXIS.md precedents.

self_qc_catches_this_session.type: domain-mismatched adversary (forcing a real number into an out-of-scope application, then catching it -- the same 'wrong tool for the job' discipline this repo's own MECHANISM_PULMONARY_GAS_EXCHANGE.md documents for DLCO-vs-DLO2)
self_qc_catches_this_session.claim: esophageal whole-transit time via a two-segment model using Pandolfino et al. 2010's fast/slow contractile-front-velocity split (CFV_fast for the proximal striated segment, CFV_slow for the entire distal segment)
self_qc_catches_this_session.initial_result: t_naive_total = 16.69s, a 66.9% overshoot vs the task's own 8-10s anchor
self_qc_catches_this_session.diagnosed_root_cause: Pandolfino et al. 2010's own abstract explicitly describes CFV_slow as reflecting PHRENIC AMPULLARY EMPTYING -- a LOCALIZED end-effect confined to the region near the LES, not a general distal-esophagus propagation rate. Applying it across the FULL distal 78.3% of esophageal length (from the 21.7% Clouse-Staiano-1991-measured transition zone to the LES) is a domain-mismatch: the ampulla is a small terminal segment, not the whole distal esophagus.
self_qc_catches_this_session.fix: use the whole-wave average velocity (Pouderoux et al. 1997, 2.5 cm/s, measured via an independent method -- endoscopic clip-tracking + strain-gauge manometry, not HRM pressure-topography) across the full length instead: L(20cm)/v(2.5cm/s) = 8.00s, inside the task's 8-10s anchor and independently corroborated by a 3rd source (Silva et al. 2018's distal-latency percentile).
self_qc_catches_this_session.note: reported as a disclosed, forced self-catch (both the naive-mismatched result AND the fix are shown in the doc/JSON), not silently discarded -- matching this repo's established 'force the adversary, catch the trap, disclose both' discipline.

self_qc_catches_this_session.type: adversary construction check (does the adversary formalization actually make the task-required adversary FAIL, or does the chosen formalism accidentally let it pass?)
self_qc_catches_this_session.claim: a 'simultaneous muscle activation' adversary (closure onset = bolus arrival exactly, zero anticipatory lead) must fail to protect the airway
self_qc_catches_this_session.initial_result: under a first, simpler formalization (protection defined purely as the GROSS apnea/closure interval containing the bolus-dwell interval, with INSTANTANEOUS closure), lead=0 STILL trivially satisfies containment (0 <= 0 and apnea_duration(1.0s) >= dwell(0.65s)) -- the adversary would NOT fail, contradicting the task's own explicit requirement
self_qc_catches_this_session.diagnosed_root_cause: treating airway closure as instantaneous is physically unrealistic -- real laryngeal-vestibule/glottal closure takes a nonzero completion latency (rise time) to actually achieve a seal. The GROSS-interval-only formalization silently assumed away exactly the mechanism that makes simultaneous activation dangerous in real physiology.
self_qc_catches_this_session.fix: added a closure-completion-latency parameter (tau_close) to the containment condition (protected iff tau_close <= lead <= margin) -- swept over [0,1.0]s rather than asserting one value, so the qualitative conclusion (simultaneous activation fails for ANY positive tau_close) does not depend on trusting a single unverified constant.
self_qc_catches_this_session.note: caught during model design, before any adversary result was reported -- an OODA loop on the model's own formalization, not on a literature claim, exactly the 'force the concept before any negative/positive' discipline applied to a modeling choice.

honest_gaps_headline: Pharyngeal model lumps the whole airway-closure apparatus into ONE proxy interval (the measured apnea interval), not a multi-muscle simulation with independently-timed velum/tongue/hyoid/larynx/glottis/UES onsets.
tau_close (closure-completion latency) and the sequenced-condition representative lead (0.15/0.20s) are illustrative, swept, NOT independently live-verified this session.
The apnea-offset/'swallow completion' landmark mapping (Martin et al. 1994) is a disclosed simplification, not a fabricated precise joint timeline.
Esophagus length (20cm) is textbook-transmitted, not independently live-verified this session -- reported as a sensitivity band [16,26]cm, not a single asserted number.
Part D's lesion-severity margin sweep is explicitly illustrative, not independently fit to patient-level dysphagia-severity data.
The Smaoui-2022-vs-Molfenter-2014 cross-study tension on which timing parameter dominates is held OPEN, not adjudicated.
Dodds et al. 1990 is bibliographic-only (no abstract text returned by efetch this session).
Achalasia's 3 HRM subtypes are not uniformly represented by the single v->0 divergent-transit-time idealization (type II retains some organized pressurization).
